questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No error'. **

On Sundays (1)/ I prefer reading (2)/ than going out visiting my friends. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer: 3**

The sentence uses ‘prefer’ incorrectly by using ‘than’, instead of ‘to’, as preferences are ranked generally. Therefore, the correct sentence would be: ‘On Sundays I prefer reading to going out visiting my friends’.

**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

P: He was a funny looking man with a high, bald, done shaped head, a face very small in comparison and a long wavy beard.

Q: He didn't work at his trade-a stonecutter, more than what was necessary to keep his wife and three boys alive.

R: His unusual features were standing a joke among his friends.

S: He was a poor man-an idler.
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer: **PRQS

The first sentence of a passage should begin with the characteristic features if a character is being introduced. Sentence P is composed of the facial and physical appearance of the character and therefore, must come first. Hence, PRQS is the correct choice out of the 4.

** In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given. **

Desecrate
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. Sanctify.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Desecrate"** means to treat (a sacred place or thing) with violent disrespect; violate. (अपवित्र करना)
 
 
• **Example: **The vandals desecrated the church by spray-painting graffiti on its walls.
 
 

 
• **"Sanctify" **means to make holy or set apart as sacred; to consecrate. (पवित्र करना)

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

P: When all the credit worthy people were given loans to a logical limit, they ceased to be a part of the market.

Q: Even this would have been understandable if it could work as an eye opener.

R: Owing to the materialistic culture elsewhere, it was possible to keep selling newer products to the consumers despite having existing ones which served equally well.

S: They were lured through advertising and marketing techniques of 'dustbinisation' of the customer; and then finally, once they became ready customers, they were given loans and credits to help them by more and more.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**RSPQ**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• We start with sentence '**R**' as it provides an introduction to the materialistic culture and the practice of constantly selling new products, establishing the context.
 
• Sentence '**S**' then follows this naturally as it details how consumers are drawn in and lured into the system of credits and loans, building upon the information given in '**R**'.
 
• '**P**' is the next logical choice, explaining the consequences of extending credit to the limit and the eventual outcome.
 
• '**Q**' finally gives a concluding remark about the situation, fitting as an ending to the paragraph.

Therefore, the correct order is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• '**PRQS**': Here, starting with 'P' does not provide a proper background or setting for the actions described in the subsequent sentences.
 
• '**QSPR**': Leading with 'Q' is incongruous, as its context relies on understanding the earlier actions and their consequences.
 
• '**RPQS**': The sequence here almost works, but having 'Q' before 'S' does not match the logical flow of events as 'Q' is more of a concluding remark.

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in ****Indirect****/Direct speech. **

He said, "I saw a snake here."

options.text: He said that he had seen a snake there.
He said that he saw a snake here.
He said that he saw a snake there.
He said that he had seen a snake.

questions.solution:
**Correct Answer: **He said that he had seen a snake there.

The sentence is in simple past recognised by "I saw" , (sub+ 2nd form of verb), which will be changed to past perfect tense and first person changes to third person . Hence option number 1 is correct as option 4 does not include the word 'there'

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence. **

There are two pens here and (either write) well.
questions.solution:
The correct sentence is **"either writes". ****
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****

 
• **‘Either writes’ **denotes that both of the pens write well.
 
• Since** 'either'** takes a *singular verb*, **‘writes’ **is used.
 
• The** present continuous tense **is used to denote an action that is going on.
 
• Structure of present continuous tense - **Subject + is/are + V₁ ing + Object.**
 
 
• For Example - She** is playing** cricket.
 
 

**Therefore, the correct sentence is** *There are two pens here and either writes well.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice. **

John was arrested on a charge of murder, but for lack of evidence, he was released.

options.text: The police arrested John on a charge of murder, but for lack of evidence released him.
John was arrested on a charge of murder but was released for lack of evidence.
The police arrested John on a charge of murder, but for lack of evidence he was released.
John had been arrested on a charge of murder, but for lack of evidence he had been released.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **The police arrested John on a charge of murder, but for lack of evidence released him.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The original sentence is in the passive voice: "John was arrested on a charge of murder, but for lack of evidence, he was released."
 
• Option 1 is the active voice alternative that maintains the original meaning: "The police arrested John on a charge of murder, but for lack of evidence released him."
 
 
• In this option, "the police" is the subject, "arrested" and "released" are the verbs, and "John" is the object. The original meaning is preserved, and the sentence structure is grammatically correct.
 
• This option best expresses the given sentence in the active voice. It conveys the same meaning as the original sentence, with the **police **as the **subject **performing the action of arresting John and subsequently releasing him due to a lack of evidence. The sentence structure follows the **active voice** format, making it the correct choice in this context.
 
 
 
• Option 2 is incorrect because it is still in the passive voice.
 
• Option 3 is incorrect because it contains a passive construction in the second half of the sentence ("he was released"). The goal is to convert the entire sentence into the active voice, which option 1 accomplishes.
 
• Option 4 is incorrect because it is also in the passive voice, and it changes the tense to past perfect ("had been arrested" and "had been released"), which is not consistent with the original sentence.
